summary: Camas County, ID firefinder on a grain elevator in Fairfield: approved in 1941, dated 1942, staffed in lightning storms; listed abandoned, not gone, and no source describes the elevator today.

facts.design: Firefinder mounted atop a grain elevator
facts.status_note: Listed as abandoned, not removed; no source says whether the elevator or firefinder still stands

events.note: Camas County commissioners approved a lookout on top of the Fairfield elevator, as quoted from the Idaho Evening Times
Firefinder placed atop the elevator, per idahofirelookouts.com's history line

corrections.why: The FFLA list reads Abandoned, not Gone, and both lookout sites also say abandoned. No source says the elevator or firefinder was removed, so gone is not supported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1941 newspaper item records the commissioners' approval of a lookout on the elevator; idahofirelookouts.com dates the firefinder to 1942; firelookout.com says 1940s. The story gives the approval year and the 1942 firefinder date separately.

notes_for_editor: The 1941 excerpt on the Forest Lookouts page is an approval, not a construction record; the 1942 date from idahofirelookouts.com is the earliest installation date in the sources. Status corrected from gone to unknown because the lists say abandoned, not removed. Nothing found on the elevator's current condition. The U of I Keeping Watch entry for Fairfield repeats the coordinates and points to firelookout.com, so it is not cited. The staffing status 'emergency' is the closest vocabulary match for 'staffed during lightning storms'. WebSearch surfaced only unrelated grain elevator fires, not used.
